slides.title: GitHub Copilot SDK
Agenda

cards.title: 1. SDK in detail
cards.text: What the runtime does; one complete agent turn; tool permissions.

cards.title: 2. SDK vs. CLI
cards.text: When an API integration is useful instead of the CLI interface.

cards.title: 3. Capabilities
cards.text: One repository assistant, developed through eight independent checkpoints.

cards.title: 4. Samples
cards.text: Run the code, inspect its results, and compare rejected and approved actions.

slides.note: Deployment variants, multi-user isolation, credential rotation, and BYOK are in the optional appendix.

slides.title: Review one repository, without changing its source
slides.lead: Our task: inspect examples/01_simple_chat.py for error handling and cleanup, then add GitHub issue context.

columns.title: With a direct model API
items: Your code sends a request and receives text or proposed tool calls.
Your code must dispatch tools, return their results, and repeat model calls.
You implement conversation state and the surrounding controls.

columns.title: With the Copilot SDK
items: The Copilot runtime manages the model/tool loop and session state.
The SDK exposes typed events, tool registration, and host callbacks.
Your application still supplies credentials and authorizes access.

slides.note: The first sample only receives a supplied repository description. It cannot inspect files until a tool is exposed.

slides.title: One user request can trigger several model calls
slides.lead: Example: ask the assistant to inspect a Python file through a custom host tool.
rows: Application → SDK
send_and_wait(prompt, timeout=60) sends the user request.
Runtime → model
Send conversation context and the available tool schemas.
Model → runtime
Propose inspect_python_file with the file argument.
Runtime → host
Request permission; the host returns an approval or rejection.
Host tool
On approval: validate the argument, read the allowed file, return AST metadata.
Runtime → model
Append the tool result to the conversation and call the model again.
Runtime → SDK
Emit the final assistant message and idle event; the wait completes.
slides.note: A rejection skips execution. Built-in tools run in the runtime; custom Python handlers run in the host. SDK assistant.turn events describe individual model iterations.

slides.title: Tool access has three separate controls

cards.title: Expose a capability
cards.text: ToolSet and available_tools select which tool schemas the model can use. Hiding a tool is not OS isolation.

cards.title: Authorize a request
cards.text: on_permission_request evaluates a proposed operation. Human input is not automatically authorization.

cards.title: Limit execution
cards.text: SandboxConfig restricts runtime-launched tools where a backend is available. Custom host handlers need separate containment.

slides.note: The workshop uses read-only tools and disposable data. A sandbox bypass intentionally removes the sandbox for one approved operation.

slides.title: Choose the interface, not a different agent engine
rows: Interface
Terminal UI; also supports non-interactive prompts.
Language API embedded in your application.
Tool interaction
CLI configuration and its built-in interaction flow.
Typed host callbacks, custom functions, and application UI.
Lifecycle
Launch and operate the CLI process.
Create sessions and own or connect to a runtime process.
Useful for
Terminal work and command-line automation.
Applications needing structured events and approval interfaces.
slides.note: Both use the Copilot runtime. The SDK is useful when parsing CLI output is not an adequate integration contract.

slides.title: Eight checkpoints for the same repository assistant
rows: Streaming session
Plan a review from supplied context; no file access yet.
Typed custom tool
Read AST metadata from an allowed Python file.
Custom agents
Research the file, then select and verify its reviewer.
Hooks
Record pre-call, success, and failure events for repository reads.
GitHub MCP
Read current issues for this repository with separate credentials.
Persistence
Recall the review file and focus in a new process.
Human approval
Choose a review focus, then approve or reject the test command.
Sandbox
Deny a private review note; allow one separately approved read.
slides.note: Each file runs independently. They are learning checkpoints, not a complete multi-user service.

slides.title: Prepare one environment and run the first checkpoint
items: Python 3.11+; the Codespace supplies Python 3.12 and the pinned packages.
These scripts use GitHub-hosted Copilot models and require Copilot access.
Use an existing Copilot CLI login or securely provision COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN.
The SDK downloads runtime 1.0.83. It does not install the interactive copilot command.

code.label: Run from the repository root
code.text:
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m copilot download-runtime
python examples/01_simple_chat.py

# Offline checks; no model requests
python -m unittest discover -s examples/tests -v

slides.note: Use the repo's Codespaces link for the prepared environment. BYOK is optional appendix material, not the default authentication for these scripts.

slides.title: Stream the review plan and require a final message
items: available_tools=[] makes this turn text-only.
Subscribe before sending; assistant.message_delta contains chunks, not guaranteed tokens.
A timeout or session error raises. An idle session without a final message returns None.
Always remove the event listener in finally.
slides.note: Run: python examples/01_simple_chat.py. This output is a plan based on supplied context, not a claim that files were inspected.

slides.title: Add a typed repository-inspection tool
items: A Pydantic parameter type defines the tool's input schema.
The handler validates an explicit file allowlist and returns AST metadata.
ToolSet exposes this custom tool without granting built-in filesystem tools.
A recorded handler invocation proves the read; the model's summary does not.
slides.note: Run: python examples/02_custom_tools.py. The complete source contains the handler and its permission policy.

slides.title: Select the reviewer and check the selected agent
items: Researcher and reviewer are configurations in one session, not parallel agents.
Both are restricted to read tools for the same repository.
Conversation context remains available when selecting the reviewer.
Check agent.name before sending the next prompt. The selection RPC is experimental.

code.label: examples/03_custom_agents.py · selection and verification
code.end: raise RuntimeError("The reviewer persona was not selected.")

slides.note: Run: python examples/03_custom_agents.py. The initial researcher selection is checked in the same way.

slides.title: Observe repository reads with hooks
items: on_pre_tool_use runs before a tool call.
on_post_tool_use handles successful execution.
on_post_tool_use_failure handles failed execution.
These handlers log tool names. They do not enforce a policy or create a sandbox.
slides.note: Run: python examples/04_hooks.py. Inspect the host trace alongside the repository answer.

slides.title: Add current GitHub issues through MCP
items: The remote GitHub MCP connection uses its own bearer credential.
Resolve the token at runtime; never print it or place it in source.
Use the read-only server header and an issue-tool allowlist.
Correlate a matching MCP start and successful completion. Zero open issues is a valid result.
slides.note: Run: python examples/05_mcp_servers.py. Copilot model login is not a replacement for MCP credentials.

slides.title: Resume the review in a second process
items: The first process stores the review file and focus in conversation context.
The second process uses the same session ID and runtime state storage.
The resume prompt must not repeat the facts being recalled.
Re-register host callbacks and tools. Session exit detaches; it does not delete saved state.
slides.note: A session ID identifies state; it is not authorization to access another user's conversation.

slides.title: Human input and permission are different requests
slides.lead: Choose a review focus, then separately authorize the fixed test command. No freeform input is inserted into shell code.

traces.title: Rejected command
traces.text:
focus: errors
approve once? n
COMMAND_DENIED id=<id>
COMMAND_DENIAL_RECORDED id=<id>
no execution claimed

traces.title: Approved command
traces.text:
focus: cleanup
approve once? y
COMMAND_APPROVE_ONCE id=<id>
COMMAND_RESULT_VERIFIED id=<id>
unittest reported OK

slides.note: Illustrative host-trace excerpts; IDs abbreviated. Command: python -m unittest discover -s examples/tests -v. Run twice with n and y. Structured input has a validated legacy fallback.

slides.title: A private review note requires a sandbox exception
slides.lead: The sample denies a disposable vault and network access. allow_bypass=True permits a request, not automatic approval.

traces.title: Rejected bypass
traces.text:
grep: private review note
approve once? n
SANDBOX_BYPASS_DENIED id=<id>
SANDBOX_DENIAL_RECORDED id=<id>
no access claimed

traces.title: Approved bypass
traces.text:
grep: content output
approve once? y
SANDBOX_BYPASS_APPROVE_ONCE id=<id>
SANDBOX_BYPASS_VERIFIED id=<id>
result contains private note

slides.note: Illustrative host-trace excerpts; IDs abbreviated. Run twice with n and y. success=True or sandboxed=True alone is not read proof. Missing backend or note content fails explicitly. Experimental API.

slides.title: Exercise: inspect another allowed file

columns.title: Change one input
items: In sample 02, choose another file from the declared allowlist.
Check the handler's AST metadata against that file.
Ask the reviewer in sample 03 about the same file.
Run sample 07 once with approval and once with rejection.

columns.title: Completion criteria
items: A real tool result supports the repository answer.
A missing final message or failed required tool is reported.
Rejected operations are not reported as successful.
The sample does not modify repository source.

slides.note: This completes the introduction. The independent checkpoints show API behavior; they do not implement tenant isolation or a production approval service.

slides.title: Managed child or existing runtime

columns.title: SDK-owned process
items: Default: provision and start the release-matched runtime over stdio.
Use RuntimeConnection.for_stdio(path=...) for an explicit executable.
Client exit stops the child it owns.

columns.title: Existing process
items: Use RuntimeConnection.for_uri(...) to connect to a running runtime.
The host protects the endpoint and owns process lifecycle.
State storage and request routing must survive reconnects.

slides.note: These are process-ownership choices. Neither choice provides application user authentication or tenant isolation.

slides.title: Application boundaries for multi-user hosting
rows: Identity and ownership
Authenticate the principal; authorize session create, resume, steering, and deletion.
State and workspaces
Separate repositories, temporary files, runtime state, and host-tool processes.
Concurrency and cancellation
Route each session to its state; bound turns, queues, duration, and resource use.
Credentials and egress
Use scoped credentials; configure each MCP connection and network boundary.
Audit
Record decisions and tool outcomes without storing credentials or private payloads.
slides.note: Shared-service deployments should review mode="empty" and explicit storage configuration rather than inheriting local workspace state.

slides.title: Credential source is not session authorization
rows: Copilot CLI login
Local signed-in user's eligible Copilot identity.
Explicit per-session token
The host supplies an eligible user's or application's credential.
Environment token
COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, or GITHUB_TOKEN; eligibility and policy still apply.
github_token_provider
Acquire and refresh short-lived Copilot credentials; do not combine with a static session token.
Generic MCP connection
Separate headers or an implemented OAuth callback; not inherited automatically from model login.
slides.note: A token's presence does not prove Copilot entitlement. Credential ownership does not replace authorization for a particular saved session.

slides.title: Configure inference with your own provider
items: ProviderConfig supplies endpoint, wire protocol, and authentication.
The model is a create_session argument, not a ProviderConfig field.
api_key, bearer_token, or bearer_token_provider depend on provider support.
Provider billing does not determine MCP credentials, tool egress, or all runtime traffic.

code.label: Configuration example · requires an eligible endpoint
code.text:
provider = ProviderConfig(
    type="openai",
    base_url=os.environ["MODEL_BASE_URL"],
    api_key=os.environ["MODEL_API_KEY"],
    wire_api="responses",
)
session = await client.create_session(
    provider=provider,
    model=os.environ["MODEL_ID"],
    available_tools=[],
)

slides.note: This is optional configuration, not the default of the eight samples. Select a compatible API and tool-capable model for your endpoint.
